title: Query Options
description: Master all major useQuery options for fine-grained control over caching, refetching, and data selection.

data.text: useQuery accepts over 20 configuration options that control every aspect of query behavior: how long data stays fresh, how retries work, when to refetch, how to transform results, and more. This lesson covers the most important options with practical examples.
staleTime and gcTime are the two most important caching options. They work together to control when data is refetched and how long unused data stays in memory.

cards.title: staleTime
cards.description: Controls when data is considered stale and eligible for refetching. While data is fresh, React Query returns it without making a network request.
pros: Prevents unnecessary refetches for stable data
Widely used for user profiles, settings
cons: Set too high and data stays outdated silently
Default is 0 â€” most beginners miss this option

cards.title: gcTime
cards.description: Controls how long unused cached data persists before being garbage-collected. Data is removed from memory after this period if no component is subscribed.
pros: Prevents memory leaks from accumulating cache entries
Allows returning to a view without a refetch (within gcTime window)
cons: Short gcTime causes unnecessary refetches on navigation

data.text: React Query refetches data automatically in several scenarios. You can fine-tune or disable each of these behaviors to match your application's needs.

data.title: Disable refetchOnWindowFocus for Sensitive Forms
data.text: If a user is filling out a form and switches tabs, refetching on window focus could overwrite their in-progress changes. Disable refetchOnWindowFocus for mutation-heavy pages.
By default, failed queries retry 3 times with exponential backoff. Configure retry and retryDelay to control error recovery behavior.

data.title: Configure a Dashboard Query
data.description: Create a Dashboard component that displays real-time server metrics. Configure useQuery options to balance freshness, performance, and user experience.
steps: Create a mock fetchMetrics function that returns server CPU, memory, and request counts
Use useQuery with queryKey ['metrics'] and a 30-second refetchInterval for live updates
Set staleTime to 10000ms so data is considered fresh for 10 seconds
Set gcTime to 1000 * 60 * 5 (5 minutes) so returning users see cached data
Use select to extract only the cpu and memory fields from the response
Show a 'Live' indicator when isFetching is true but data is already displayed
Configure retry: 1 and show a 'Reconnecting...' message on error
data.expectedOutcome: A dashboard that updates every 30 seconds while the tab is active, shows stale data gracefully during refetches, and reconnects silently on transient errors.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: staleTime controls when data is refetched â€” higher = fewer network requests
gcTime controls how long unused data stays in cache
refetchOnWindowFocus, refetchOnMount, and refetchOnReconnect control automatic refetching triggers
retry and retryDelay configure error recovery behavior
select transforms data before it reaches your component
refetchInterval enables polling for live data
All options can be set globally (defaultOptions) or per-query
data.takeaway: Query options give you fine-grained control over every aspect of the data-fetching lifecycle. Start with defaults and tune each option based on your data's freshness requirements.
